subject: Mathematical Thinking
goal: Take an English mathematical claim, write its formal skeleton, know what a proof of it must do — the human-language groundwork for formalizing maths in Lean. Ends on the completeness of the reals, where intuition fails and precision rescues.

learner.owns: Solid high-school mathematics — algebra, equations, roots, functions, trig, basic calculus as procedures. No proof experience.
learner.lean: little or none assumed; every Lean snippet introduced from scratch

source: transcripts/LN7cCW1rSsI.txt — Keith Devlin, Introduction to Mathematical Thinking (Stanford)

cruxes.title: Why precision isn't fussiness
cruxes.hook: A five-line chain of algebra you can check yourself that ends at 1 = −1. Every link looks fine. Find the broken one.
cruxes.crux: A statement must have exactly one truth value, independent of reader and context — because a proof is a chain, and a link that can be read two ways is not a link.
cruxes.owns: Everyday language, and school algebra with square roots.
cruxes.pays: The four linguistic forms + three combinators: the finite alphabet all mathematical statements are built from. This is the map of the whole ladder.

cruxes.title: The implication table is forced, not chosen
cruxes.hook: Build the truth table for 'if φ then ψ' yourself. Watch every alternative to the standard one die.
cruxes.crux: Once you demand that a compound statement's truth depend only on the truth of its parts, the material conditional is the only survivor. 'False implies anything' is not a convention.
cruxes.owns: Crux 1's definite truth value, and the combinators and/or/not.
cruxes.pays: Mechanical computation of truth — and the table that will later license proof by contradiction.

cruxes.title: Quantifier order is meaning
cruxes.hook: A cancer foundation's fact sheet that accidentally condemns one man to die every hour, forever.
cruxes.crux: Nesting order of ∀ and ∃ changes what is claimed. Negation is then a crank: push ¬ inward, every quantifier flips.

cruxes.title: The form of a statement is the proof's blueprint
cruxes.hook: Two statements you cannot yet prove. Read only their shapes, and write the first three lines of each proof anyway.
cruxes.crux: The logical form dictates the proof's moves: ∀ says take an arbitrary one, ∃ says produce one, → says assume the antecedent. No template hunting.
cruxes.pays: The Lean-shaped skill — intro, use, apply are these moves.

cruxes.title: The indirect moves, and why they're legal
cruxes.hook: Proof by contradiction feels like cheating. Derive your licence to use it from a truth table you already built.
cruxes.crux: Contradiction, contrapositive and induction are not tricks handed down; each is licensed by something already established.
cruxes.pays: √2 is irrational, proved and understood — and induction as a move you could have invented.

cruxes.title: The hole in the rationals
cruxes.hook: The fractions look like they fill the number line completely. Prove that they don't.
cruxes.crux: Completeness: a set of rationals plainly bounded above with no least upper bound in the rationals. Intuition fails; the machinery holds.
cruxes.pays: Why anyone built any of this.
